___ year-old female with a history of DMII, CVA ___, seizure,

COPD,  C diff, MRSA bacteremia, multiple UTI's who is admitted 
for N&V with concern for RLL aspiration pneumonia.

#) suspected RLL pneumonia: per CXr read, history of aspiration 
pneumonia and new leukocytosis on admission.

Patient was 
clinically stable w/ good saturations, no respiratory distress 
and afebile throughout admission.

Urine leginella Ag was 
negative.

Bcx were negative to date with fional results still 
pending at discharge.

Patient was seen by speechand swallow who 
did not find tendency to aspirate and recommended regular diet.

She was initially treated with IV Vanco + Ceftriaxone + PO 
azithro, then as was doing clinically wel transitioned to PO

Cefpodoxine + Azithromycin and remained afebrile and stable with 
this.
Post Discharge plan:

- oral cefpodoxine and azithromycine as below for completion of 
total 7 day course.
- repeat CXR in 6 weeks.

#) Nausea/vomitting: Patient has long history of recurrent bouts 
of N&V. Current bout may have been ___ to her lung infection.

Patient does has hx of c.dif but no abdominal pain or diarrhea 
and c.dif toxin was negative.

Cultures for viral gastroenteritis 
were sent on admission and were NTD at the time of discharge, 
final results are still pending.

ACS was ruled out per CE neg X2 
and non ichemic ECG.
She did have minimal elevation of AST and
ALKP which trended down subsequently, her GGT was also elevated,
T.bili and lipase were normal.

She had more significant 
elevations on previous admission which subsequently resolved.

Workup in the past included CT abdomen and RUQ US which 
demonstrated cholecystolithiasis w/o cholecystis or bile duct 
dilatation.

CT of the abdomen on this admission did not show 
evidence of acute intra-abdominal event, gallblader stones or 
other concerning finding.

Patient recurrent episodes of V+N may 
thus may concievebly be due to  gastroparesis in a diabetic 
patient and/or biliary colic.

Given her various comorbidities 
she would not be a candidate for cholecystectomy.

Management 
would thus be symptomatic.

A gastric emptying study may be 
considered in the out patient setting.
Post Discharge Plan:
- consider gastric emptying study
